svg.text: Selection moves the behavior; the OLMo risk model's self-description barely moves
Each dot is one selection-loop rollout of the OLMo risk model (K2 chassis). Change = final round minus round 0, on two probes run at the same checkpoints:
behavior = P(choose the riskier option) on held-out EV-neutral A/B gambles; stated = P(describes itself as the risk-tolerant one), order-balanced forced choice.
A. Behavior change against stated change, one dot per moved rollout
change in risk behavior over the rollout (final round minus round 0)
change in stated risk tolerance (final round minus round 0)
K2 judge grid: frozen, self, random (9 moved)
moved less than 0.15 — excluded from fit (12)
B. Stated movement per unit of behavior movement,
Tracking ratio = (change in stated tolerance) divided by
(change in behavior) for each rollout whose behavior moved by
at least 0.15, averaged within the condition group. The
best-tracking group recovers a seventh of perfect tracking;
The direction of the tiny stated shifts does follow the behavior, but at
roughly one-twentieth the size (correlation r = 0.78). Press-depth runs
hold a cautious frozen judge for one to four rounds, then release to the
